subject: Getting wrong when running log-normal distribution

messages.author: 46d394676a1f51e8
messages.subject: Getting wrong when running log-normal distribution
parts:
Hi Stan developers,

The code is running wrong when I do a simple log-normal model. Can you help me to have a look? Thank you.
My computer system is windows 8.1 and running Stan (2.2.0) on R x64 3.1.0. Here is my simple Rstan model, initial values and warning.
If you wanna the data to check where wrong is, I will send to you in privacy. Thank you so much again. 

Rstan model:
data {
    int<lower=0> n;
    real y[n];
}

parameters {

  real<lower=0> sigma;

  real mu;
}

model {

 y[n] ~ normal(mu,sigma);
}

initial values: initval<-list(list(sigma=7.18,mu=1.30)
              )

warning is like this: "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Scale parameter is -1.#IND:0, but must be > 0!
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."

Best,
Hang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Getting wrong when running log-normal distribution
parts:
On Aug 3, 2014, at 12:21 PM, Hang Zeng <caff...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Stan developers,
>
> The code is running wrong when I do a simple log-normal model. Can you help me to have a look? Thank you.
> My computer system is windows 8.1 and running Stan (2.2.0) on R x64 3.1.0. Here is my simple Rstan model, initial values and warning.
> If you wanna the data to check where wrong is, I will send to you in privacy. Thank you so much again.
>
> Rstan model:
> data {
> int<lower=0> n;
> real y[n];
> }
>
> parameters {
>
> real<lower=0> sigma;
>
> real mu;
> }
>
> model {
>
> y[n] ~ normal(mu,sigma);
> }

The above can't be the model that produced the message below.

In the model block, the variable n will only use the very last
value, which isn't enough to pin down sigma. What you want to do is:

for (i in 1:n)
y[i] ~ normal(mu,sigma);

or better yet, just vectorize and write this:

y ~ normal(mu,sigma);

This isn't a lognormal model, by the way.

- Bob

>
> initial values: initval<-list(list(sigma=7.18,mu=1.30)
> )
>
> warning is like this: "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
> Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Scale parameter is -1.#IND:0, but must be > 0!
> If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
> but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."
>
> Best,
> Hang

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Getting wrong when running log-normal distribution
parts:
The key words in that error message is "If this warning occurs sporadically…". While Drs. Gelman, Goodrich, and Betancourt can explain this much more rigorously, sometimes, the sampler picks a value that is illegal when it "jumps" around. If this is infrequent, it isn't a big deal. If it is constant, you may want to think about re-parameterizing the model.

Avi
